**Per-task check 4 — handling time.** Two writes, two moments:

- *Moment A* — the grant. All of its prerequisites are resolved (it has none:
  `trips_ext_mileage_topup_grant.prerequisite: []`, line 1111), and it is not yet written. The world
  is `initial_state` exactly, at `NOW = 2026-09-18`. Every binding of `granted_miles` is evaluated
  there.
- *Moment B* — the purchase. Its one prerequisite is resolved, so the world is `initial_state` plus
  the real DB effect of the grant write — one `trips_usage` row with
  `event_type='trips_mileage_allowance_granted'`, `grant_reason='purchased_package'`,
  `usage_date='2026-09-18'`, `usage_source='guest_report'`, `reading_point='mid_trip'`,

No formula is evaluated early. In particular `granted_miles` at Moment B reads
`SUM('trips_usage','miles_delta', event_type='trips_mileage_allowance_granted',
grant_reason='purchased_package')` (line 1323), which is `0` at Moment A and only becomes the grant
figure at Moment B — the prerequisite is genuinely consumed at the later moment, not anticipated.
Neither persona nor tool fallback substitutes for an eligibility judgement: the tool bodies make no
judgement at all. **PASS.**

**Per-task check 5 — no real-world waits.** Every fact both writes consume is either an

**Consequence of the charter-global defects on this task's own world.**

*F-01 (undeclared override of the per-booking included-mile ceiling).* Both readings are defensible
from the rendered charter, and they give different scored values on this world:

| reading | `mile_ceiling` | `granted_to_date` | `headroom` | `granted_miles` | `purchase_amount` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| extended `included_mile_ceiling_tier` t1 (reserved period 66 days ≥ 60, no overage on this reservation) | 8000 | 3750 | 4250 | **3600** | **$814.40** |
| base trips.yaml:739 + Monthly `included_miles_cap_per_booking` (trips.yaml:214) | 3750 | 3750 | 0 | **0** | **$0.00** |

The base reading is not a straw man: the booking's own `included_miles_total` is `3750`
(`initial_state.trips_bookings["9c741700-…"].included_miles_total`), which is exactly the Monthly
plan's published per-booking cap, and the base sentence forecloses a longer-reservation exception in
so many words ("however long the reservation runs"). An agent that follows it grants nothing and
charges nothing. Task 0 therefore has a second defensible answer on both of its scored parameters.

*F-02 (undeclared override of the published block price).* Holding every other binding at the
extended reading and substituting only the base's published `extra_miles_package_price` for the
Keyturn Monthly Rate Plan ($145.00 per 500-mile block, trips.yaml:215):
`net_block_price = 145 − 8 = 137`, `line_price = RND(3600 × 137/500, 2) = 986.40`,
`result = RND(MX(0, 986.40 + 12 − 40), 2) = ` **$958.40** against the extended **$814.40**. A second
defensible answer on `purchase_amount`. (Read the base package clause more literally still — whole
packages only, 8 packages of 500 at $145 — and the figure is $1,160.00.)

*F-06 (cross-difficulty rows contradict the guestplan charter).* Demonstrated in `factor_weight`
below.

### problem_chain

Walked from the root problem using the policy and the world only.

**Root.** `user_scenario` asks for one thing: *"the included miles on this rental are nearly gone …
she would rather buy more miles now than be hit with a per-mile bill at the end of the trip. She
asks the desk to sort out a top-up on the rental and put it on the card the trip is already running
on."* The money she is asking to pay is `purchase_amount`, whose policy is
`trips_ext_mileage_topup_pricing` (`computes: purchase_amount`, line 1270) and whose write is the
guest's own (`pay_for_mileage_topup_d571ad94`, `owner="user"`, task_tools.py:47). **Root problem =
`trips_ext_mileage_topup_pricing`.**

**Its prerequisite sentences.** Reading the root policy's own `rule` (lines 1295–1304), one sentence
joins its result to something else with an ordering connective — line 1296, second sentence:
*"The price of a mileage top-up is fixed **only after** the miles it adds stand on the reservation's
included-mile record."* No other sentence of that rule states an order.

**Does that state hold at `frozen_time`?** No. `initial_state.trips_usage` holds five rows for
booking `9c741700-7c1a-44fc-b463-4db182e7e04c`:

| usage_id | event_type | usage_date | grant_reason | miles_delta | usage_source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `7cec7ea6-…` | `trips_mileage_allowance_granted` | 2026-07-30 | **`plan_allowance`** | +3750 | telematics |
| `b3ad3cb6-…` | `trips_fuel_level_recorded` | 2026-08-05 | none | 0 | telematics |
| `f46ba239-…` | `trips_mileage_usage_recorded` | 2026-08-19 | none | −1150 | telematics |
| `7b132734-…` | `trips_mileage_usage_recorded` | 2026-09-04 | none | −1100 | telematics |
| `dd325c51-…` | `trips_mileage_usage_recorded` | 2026-09-16 | none | −550 | **host_report** |

No row carries `grant_reason='purchased_package'`, i.e. no top-up's miles stand on the record. The
state the sentence waits on is **false at the opening**. Evidence path:
`tasks/0.json → initial_state.trips_usage.*` filtered on
`booking_id = "9c741700-7c1a-44fc-b463-4db182e7e04c"`.

**Which write brings it about?** The sentence is in the state form and does not say. Reading the
other policies' rules, `trips_ext_mileage_topup_grant` opens (line 1099) "A guest who asks for more
included miles part way through a reservation **is granted a top-up of included miles**, and how
many miles that top-up adds is worked out as follows", and its `target_tool` is
`grant_mileage_topup_0373887d`, whose body creates exactly a
`trips_mileage_allowance_granted` / `purchased_package` row (task_tools.py:39–42). No other policy of
this difficulty writes such a row. One candidate, so the hop resolves.

**Its own prerequisite sentences.** `trips_ext_mileage_topup_grant.rule` (lines 1098–1110) contains
no ordering connective joining its result to another problem, and `prerequisite: []` (line 1111)
agrees. The walk terminates.

**The tree the auditor derives:**

```
trips_ext_mileage_topup_pricing   (root, computes purchase_amount, owner=user)
        ^
        | kind = value_input, gate = granted_miles, form = state
        |
trips_ext_mileage_topup_grant     (computes granted_miles, owner=agent)
```

- nodes: 2 · prerequisite problems: n = 1 (within 1–3) · `value_input` edges: 1 ≥ max(n−1, 1) = 1
- cycles: none
- topological order: `grant_mileage_topup_0373887d` → `pay_for_mileage_topup_d571ad94`
- at least one problem is the customer's own write: the **root** is
  (`pay_for_mileage_topup_d571ad94`, `owner="user"`, task_tools.py:47), and the persona hands it over
  passively — *"Once the agent has set the payment up and handed it over to her, she completes it
  herself there and then"*.

**Isomorphic to the declared tree?** The `prerequisite` block of
`trips_ext_mileage_topup_pricing` (lines 1305–1316) declares exactly this single edge with
`kind: value_input`, `gate: granted_miles`, `form: state`,
`resolved_by: grant_mileage_topup_0373887d`. Same nodes, same edge, same kind, same direction.
**Isomorphic.**

**Per-edge load-bearing run.** Skip the grant write and replay the purchase unchanged on
`initial_state`: `granted_miles` = `SUM(trips_usage.miles_delta where
event_type='trips_mileage_allowance_granted' and grant_reason='purchased_package')` = **0.0**;
`concession` falls to the fall-through (0.00); `line_price` takes the second tier (reserved period
66 days ≥ 60, granted < 2000) and returns `RND(int(0/500) × 125, 2)` = 0.00; `handling_charge` = 12.00;
`early_credit` = 40.00; `result` = `RND(MX(0, 0 + 12 − 40), 2)` = **$0.00** against the gold
**$814.40**. The edge changes the scored value by the whole of it. **Bears weight.**

**Parallel edges / terminal state.** The root has exactly one out-edge, so there is no pair of writes
sharing a balance, a cap or a dedup key whose order the policy would have to pin down. The terminal
state is unambiguous: one new `trips_usage` grant row and one new `trips_charges` line of
`charge_basis='extra_miles_package'`, in that order.

**No-wait argument.** Both resolving actions complete synchronously in the conversation (see
check 5 above). The grant is the desk's own call; the purchase is the guest's call at the desk's
hand-over, and the persona commits to making it — *"she completes it herself there and then, and
reads the confirmation back if she is asked to"*.

**The tool layer judges no prerequisite.** `grant_mileage_topup_0373887d` is
`ctx.make_id` + `ctx.create` + a confirmation string (task_tools.py:38–44);
`pay_for_mileage_topup_d571ad94` likewise (task_tools.py:72–80). Neither reads any other row,
neither raises, neither branches, neither hints. Calling the purchase first would succeed and simply
price a top-up that is not there — the environment does not make the decision for the agent.

### task_independent_derivation

**Now / wait / refuse: act now.** `frozen_time = 2026-09-18 10:40:00 UTC`. The booking
`9c741700-…` is `status: in_progress`, its reserved period runs 2026-08-05 → 2026-10-09, and the
guest is asking mid-trip. Base eligibility clears in both directions:
`allowance_window_open` (trips.yaml:746–758) allows an allowance record while the reservation is
`booked | in_progress | completed` — it is `in_progress`; `booking_open_for_pricing`
(trips.yaml:710–722) allows a priced line while the reservation is
`requested | booked | in_progress` — it is `in_progress`. Nothing is waiting on a future date or a
third party. **Act now.**

**The object.** The narrowest business object is booking
`9c741700-7c1a-44fc-b463-4db182e7e04c`, not the guest's portfolio. The guest holds a second
booking, `dd2889df-3d5d-4f5d-a813-a2ad339c252f` (Keyturn Weekend Rate Plan, `settled`,
2026-05-22 → 2026-05-25), which base `trips_agg_multi_holding` (trips.yaml:614–621) keeps entirely
separate — "Each reservation is a contract in its own right … nothing is netted between two
reservations". Correlation key: `booking_id`. Every aggregate in both computations is
holding-scoped, so the settled booking's rows are excluded by the rule, not by chance.

**Reachability of every input.** `find_customers(phone_number="2065512238")` → the single profile
(the persona volunteers the mobile first); `find_trips_bookings(customer_id=…)` → both bookings, the
in-progress one identified by the dates the persona states ("it started on the fifth of August and
runs through to the ninth of October"); `find_trips_usage(booking_id=…)` → the five usage rows,
including `usage_source` ("a telematics figure and a figure the host or guest reported can be told
apart", share_tools.py:110–112); `find_trips_charges(booking_id=…)` → the three charge lines;
`find_guestplan_elections(booking_id=…)` → the election; `find_guestplan_charges(booking_id=…)` →
the two protection-fee rows. Every query parameter comes from earlier reachable information. The
persona has a definite answer to everything a real agent must ask, and volunteers nothing about
policy: *"She does not know what extra miles cost, does not know how the marketplace decides how
many miles to add, and will not guess at either."*

**Authorisation boundary.** The persona authorises the agent to compute and to arrange
(*"she is happy for the agent to work out what it comes to"*) and reserves the payment to herself
(*"she will do whatever has to be done at her end to pay for it"*). That maps exactly onto
`owner=agent` for the grant and `owner=user` for the purchase. She closes where the work closes:
*"She rings off only when she has heard both that the miles are on the rental and that the payment
went through."* The persona raises only the root problem and never names, hints at or asks about the
grant as a separate step, and issues no other item of work.

| `included_mile_ceiling_tier` | parameter | yes — 8000 / 4500 / 3750 | t1 | 66 d ≥ 60 **and** no mileage overage on this reservation | `trips_charges` holds no `mileage_overage` row for `9c741700-…` | "the standard ceiling being three thousand seven hundred and fifty miles" → 3750 | yes, `K('ceiling_standard')` = 3750 | **0** (≠ 3600) |
| `top_up_reserve_tier` | parameter | yes — 800 / 400 / 0 | t2 | 66 d ≥ 60 **and** readings booked 2800 ≤ 3000 | the three usage rows | "the standard top-up reserve is nil" → 0 | yes, `K('reserve_standard')` = 0 | **2700** (≠ 3600) |

All six **bear weight**. Counts: 6 factors (within 4–6), 4 `parameter` (≥ 2), 2 `method` (≥ 1).

*Whole-baseline fall-back.* Substituting all six baselines at once:
`miles_unused = 1500`, `days_covered = 21`, `daily_allowance = 125`, `block_size = 500`,
`mile_ceiling = 3750`, `reserve_miles = 0` → `shortfall = MX(0, 21×125 − 1500 + 0) = 1125`,
`blocks = ⌈1125/500⌉ = 3`, `granted_raw = 1500`, `headroom = MX(0, 3750 − 3750) = 0`,
`result` = **0**. Definite, and different from gold. Recorded with the reservation at
`_difficulty.md` §`findings` **O-01**: the number is definite but reads as a refusal.

*Stamp check.* No field in `initial_state` names any of these six outcomes. `included_miles_total`
(3750) is the granted total, not a ceiling tier; `miles_remaining` (1500) is the standing figure the
`unused_miles_basis` fall-through uses, i.e. the **baseline's** input, not the tier's — and the
gold tier deliberately departs from it. `usage_source` names the provenance of a reading, not a
tier. No tier can be read off a stamp. **PASS.**

*Near-miss.* Record `trips_charges["7b8325ec-7b98-4427-a631-6cccc9d77b62"]`:
`charge_basis: "mileage_overage"`, `charge_amount: 28.0`, `charge_date: 2026-05-26`,
`booking_id: "dd2889df-3d5d-4f5d-a813-a2ad339c252f"` — a genuine mileage overage charged to **this
guest**, on her **other** booking. A careless reader counts it, takes
`included_mile_ceiling_tier` tier 2, and computes `mile_ceiling = 4500`,
`headroom = 750`, `granted_miles = ` **750** instead of 3600 — and then `purchase_amount` = $178.75
instead of $814.40. The rule excludes it in words: "no mileage overage has been charged **on the
reservation**" (line 1109), and base `trips_agg_multi_holding` (trips.yaml:618–619) makes the same
point generally. Secondary near-misses on the same computation: the other booking's own allowance
grant (`56979f77`, +750) and return reading (`9733e0f4`, −835), which a reader who aggregates by
`customer_id` instead of `booking_id` would fold into `ledger_unused` and `driven_miles`. **PASS —
one genuine near-miss, and it flips a tier.**

**Computation B — `trips_ext_mileage_topup_pricing`, `purchase_amount`, gold $814.40.**

| factor | label | tiers differ in that kind? | tier taken | conditions satisfied | raw rows | `baseline.rule` gives | `baseline` honest? | scored value under that baseline |

All five **bear weight**. Counts: 5 factors, 4 `parameter`, 1 `method`.

*Whole-baseline fall-back.* `block_price = 145`, `concession = 0`, `line_price = ⌈3600/500⌉ × 145 =
1160.00`, `handling_charge = 6`, `early_credit = 0` → `result` = **$1,166.00**. Definite, different
from gold.

*Stamp check.* No `initial_state` field names a block price, a concession band, a line-price basis, a
handling band or a credit band. **PASS.**

*Near-miss.* Same near-miss family as computation A carries over into `driven_miles_a` (the other
booking's −835 reading) and `latest_source` (the fuel reading `b3ad3cb6` of 2026-08-05, which a
reader who does not filter on `event_type='trips_mileage_usage_recorded'` might treat as a reading —
it is telematics, and counting it would not change the tier here, but it is the kind of row the
filter is for). The load-bearing near-miss for this computation is
`trips_charges["7b8325ec-…"]` reached through the grant it changes. **PASS.**

*Multi-source and cross-difficulty over the task's computations.* Multi-source: satisfied many times
over — every non-fall-through tier of all eleven factors above conjoins conditions over at least two
distinct records (booking dates × usage ledger, booking dates × charges ledger, election × guestplan
ledger). Cross-difficulty: `protection_block_price` decides its tier from the guest's **guestplan**
holding and ledger, and those rows are present in `initial_state`
(`guestplan_elections["4ef510a7-…"]`, `guestplan_charges["0093eb01-…"]`, `["f71a55e4-…"]`).
**Counts satisfied.**

*But the cross-difficulty rows contradict the guestplan charter* — `_difficulty.md` §`findings`
**F-06**. Demonstrated here on this task's world: the election is
`Keyturn Business Traveler Protection`, whose charter parameters are
`daily_protection_fee_amount: 64.0` on a `daily_flat` basis with
`protection_fee_minimum_amount: 64.0` (`blueprint/products/guestplan.yaml`). Each seeded
protection-fee row covers `days_covered: 22` and charges `168.0`, i.e. **$7.64 a day** where the
guest's own level charges **$64.00 a day**; the charter-correct figure for a single such row is
`22 × 64 = $1,408.00`. `elec_fees` is therefore 336.00 where the guestplan charter would make it
2,816.00. Recomputed on the charter-correct figure the tier is unchanged (both clear the $200.00
threshold) and `purchase_amount` stays **$814.40**, so no scored number moves; what fails is that
the factor's cross-difficulty evidence is not evidence about that product at all.

## findings

---

**Finding 0-A — SOURCE-POLICY RED — the per-booking included-mile ceiling has two answers on this
task's world.**

*Verdict.* Red light. Charter-global root cause recorded once at
`_difficulty.md` §`findings` **F-01**; demonstrated here against task 0's world and scored solution.

*Symptom.* Two clauses of the rendered charter fix the reservation's included-mile ceiling at
different figures, and the agent's scored numbers follow whichever it reads.

*Root cause.* `trips_ext_mileage_topup_grant` declares one `overwrite` entry naming the base
package-purchase sentence, and leaves the base ceiling sentence standing while contradicting it.
See `_difficulty.md` §`override_declarations` and §`findings` F-01 for the quotations.

*Evidence.* `blueprint/products/trips.yaml:739` + Monthly `included_miles_cap_per_booking: 3750`
(trips.yaml:214) against `trips.extended.yaml:1109` + `params.ceiling_long_clean: 8000` (line 1084);
`tasks/0.json initial_state.trips_bookings["9c741700-…"].included_miles_total = 3750`;
`initial_state.trips_usage["7cec7ea6-…"].miles_delta = 3750`.
`design_rationale`'s claim that the base policy's other clauses "stay in force and are inherited"
is the author's own assertion that this conflict does not exist.

*Demonstrated consequence.* Recomputed on this world: under the extended tier,
`mile_ceiling = 8000`, `headroom = 4250`, `granted_miles = 3600`, `purchase_amount = $814.40` (GT).
Under the base sentence, `mile_ceiling = 3750`, `headroom = 0`, `granted_miles = 0`,
`purchase_amount = $0.00`. Both are defensible from the documents the rollout sees; the task
therefore has a second answer on **both** of its scored parameters, and the second answer is the
whole of the task rather than a rounding difference.

*Affected artifact and location.* `tasks/trip_booking_and_settlement_desk/trips.extended.yaml`
`trips_ext_mileage_topup_grant.overwrite` (lines 1066–1071), `params` (lines 1083–1085), `rule`
line 1109, factor `included_mile_ceiling_tier` (lines 1219–1233); and the scored solution
`tasks/0.json computations[0].expected` (3600) and `computations[1].expected` (814.4).

*Relation to previous revisions.* New; revision 1.

---

**Finding 0-B — SOURCE-POLICY RED — the price of a block of extra miles has two answers on this
task's world.**

*Verdict.* Red light. Charter-global root cause recorded once at `_difficulty.md` §`findings`
**F-02**; demonstrated here.

*Symptom.* The marketplace's published price for a block of extra miles on the Keyturn Monthly Rate
Plan and the price this policy charges differ, and nothing declares the difference.

*Root cause.* `trips_ext_mileage_topup_pricing` carries `overwrite: []` and omits
`trips_evt_mileage_allowance` — the base policy carrying `extra_miles_package_price` — from
`base_policy_refs`. See `_difficulty.md` §`findings` F-02 for the quotations.

*Evidence.* `blueprint/products/trips.yaml:52` and :215
(`extra_miles_package_price: 145.00`, `extra_miles_package_size_miles: 500` for the Monthly plan,
reaching the policy through trips.yaml:765) against `trips.extended.yaml:1274`
(`block_price_corporate: 125.00`) and :1300.

*Demonstrated consequence.* Recomputed on this world with every other binding held at the extended
reading: `net_block_price = 145 − 8 = 137`, `line_price = RND(3600 × 137/500, 2) = 986.40`,
`purchase_amount = RND(MX(0, 986.40 + 12 − 40), 2) = ` **$958.40** against the scored **$814.40**.
(GT's own `factor_sensitivity` records the same $958.40 as the `protection_block_price` baseline,
which is exactly the base figure — so the artifact itself computes the base reading and files it as
a baseline rather than as a conflict.)

*Affected artifact and location.* `trips.extended.yaml` `trips_ext_mileage_topup_pricing`
`base_policy_refs` (line 1266), `overwrite` (line 1267), `params` (lines 1273–1275), `rule`
line 1300; scored solution `tasks/0.json computations[1].expected` (814.4).

*Relation to previous revisions.* New; revision 1.

---

**Finding 0-C — SOURCE-FACTOR RED — this task's cross-difficulty evidence could not exist under the
guestplan charter.**

*Verdict.* Red light. Charter-global root cause recorded once at `_difficulty.md` §`findings`
**F-06**; demonstrated here.

*Symptom.* The only `cross_difficulty` factor of this task, `protection_block_price`, decides its
tier from guestplan ledger rows whose amounts the guestplan charter does not permit.

*Root cause.* The guestplan rows seeded into `tasks/0.json initial_state` charge a protection fee
that does not follow from the elected level's own parameters.

*Evidence.* `initial_state.guestplan_elections["4ef510a7-0d9a-4244-b220-138d89affb13"]
.protection_level_name = "Keyturn Business Traveler Protection"`;
`initial_state.guestplan_charges["0093eb01-…"]` and `["f71a55e4-…"]`, each
`charge_basis: "daily_protection_fee"`, `charge_amount: 168.0`, `days_covered: 22`.
`blueprint/products/guestplan.yaml`, Keyturn Business Traveler Protection:
`daily_protection_fee_amount: 64.0`, `protection_fee_charging_basis: daily_flat`,
`protection_fee_minimum_amount: 64.0`. 168.0 ÷ 22 = **$7.64 a day** against a charter daily flat of
**$64.00**; a charter-correct row would be 22 × 64 = **$1,408.00**.

*Demonstrated consequence.* The factor's `elec_fees` is 336.00 where the other product's own charter
would make it 2,816.00 — the read returns a figure that product never produced, so the factor tests
nothing about it. Recomputed at the charter-correct figure the $200.00 threshold is still cleared
and `purchase_amount` remains $814.40, so **no scored number moves**; what is defective is the
evidence the factor rests on, not the arithmetic. Note also that `guestplan_elections[…]
.protection_fee_balance_due = 336.0` mirrors the same impossible total.

*Affected artifact and location.* `tasks/trip_booking_and_settlement_desk/tasks/0.json`
`initial_state.guestplan_charges` (both rows) and `initial_state.guestplan_elections["4ef510a7-…"]`;
factor `protection_block_price` in `trips.extended.yaml` (lines 1357–1371).

*Relation to previous revisions.* New; revision 1.

---

**Observation 0-D — the persona pre-empts the ruling of a scored factor.**

`user_scenario`: *"She half remembers the app telling her she still had about 1500 included miles,
but she says herself that the figure has not moved in a while and cannot be right after the driving
she has done, **so she asks for it to be checked against the record rather than taken from what she
saw**."* The choice between the figure standing on the reservation (`miles_remaining = 1500`) and a
figure reconstructed from the mileage record (950) is precisely what the `unused_miles_basis` factor
decides, and it is worth 900 miles and $76.40 on this task (baseline 2700 against gold 3600). The
persona states the factor's conclusion, though not its conditions.

Recorded as an **observation and not a red light**: the conditions the ladder actually turns on
(44 days run ≥ 28, three readings ≥ 3) are objectively on the record and an agent reaches the same
tier from the policy alone, so the persona is redundant with the policy rather than a substitute for
it, and it neither creates a second reading nor removes one. GT's own `prerequisite_closure
.no_user_hint` acknowledges the line — "the closest she comes to the records is doubting the
unused-mile figure she half remembers from the app and asking for it to be checked" — and is correct
that it does not name the prerequisite. The observation is about the factor, not the tree.

---

**Observation 0-E — inherited from the charter.**

`_difficulty.md` §`findings` **O-01** (the topup-grant baseline publishes a refusal, and this task's
`baseline_result` of `0` is that refusal) and **O-05** (the `protection_block_price` ladder's tiers
overlap as stated; no election in this world is voided, so the overlap is not realised here).
